scenario: A 52-year-old male with diabetes, hypertension, hypothyroidism, dyslipidemia, and end-stage renal disease on hemodialysis presents with weakness and dizziness after missing dialysis. He has an idioventricular rhythm with ECG findings concerning for hyperkalemia, and deterioration occurs if calcium is not given promptly.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a 12-lead ECG now. He's bradycardic at 50 with an idioventricular rhythm and I need it characterized.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Give atropine 0.5 mg IV now. He's symptomatic bradycardic in the 40s with an idioventricular rhythm and a pressure of 87/62.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Atropine 0.5 mg IV in.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: ECG's back — reads hyperkalemia STEMI mimic, idioventricular rhythm. HR still 48, BP 87/62, no response to the atropine. Glucose 12.7.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Calcium gluconate IV now. This is hyperkalemia — idioventricular rhythm, no response to atropine. I need cardiac membrane stabilization.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Calcium gluconate is going in now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Insulin with dextrose IV now to shift the potassium. The calcium stabilized the membrane but it doesn't lower his potassium.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Insulin and dextrose are in for the hyperkalemia. I'll keep monitoring glucose and the cardiac tracing.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Repeat 12-lead ECG now. He's back in sinus at 66 with a better pressure — I want to confirm the hyperkalemic changes are resolving after the calcium and insulin/dextrose.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Get me a venous blood gas now — I need to confirm the potassium is actually coming down after the calcium and insulin/dextrose.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Both back. Repeat ECG is NSR, no ST changes. But the gas still shows K 8.6 — potassium hasn't come down. pH 7.27, HCO3 20, lactate 2.5, glucose 12.7, Na 142. He needs definitive potassium removal.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: Potassium's still 8.6 despite the calcium and insulin/dextrose — shifting isn't cutting it. Start sodium zirconium cyclosilicate for definitive removal, and get nephrology on the phone now for urgent dialysis.

messages.content: Your potassium is dangerously high and I need to know why. What medical problems do you have and what medications are you on — any kidney disease or dialysis you've missed?

messages.speaker: patient
messages.content: I'm scared... I feel really weak and dizzy, lightheaded, no energy, and sick to my stomach. I have diabetes, high blood pressure, an underactive thyroid, and high cholesterol. I take ramipril, levothyroxine, insulin, and Crestor. I don't know about any kidney disease or dialysis. I haven't passed any water. No chest pain and I'm not having trouble breathing.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: High-dose nebulized salbutamol now — another shifting agent while we wait, because his potassium is still 8.6 and not budging. And confirm nephrology is en route for urgent dialysis.

messages.speaker: nurse
messages.content: Salbutamol nebulizer for the hyperkalemia is running now.

messages.speaker: clinician
messages.content: I need to be straight with you. Your potassium is still 8.6 - dangerously high - despite everything we've given. Those medications only shift it around temporarily; they don't actually remove it. The fact that you haven't passed any urine, combined with your ramipril, tells me your kidneys are failing. The only thing that will truly clear this is dialysis, and the kidney specialists are on their way now for that.
